record.original_question: For a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in R^3 whose boundary is a planar closed curve C, what hypotheses on the boundary guarantee that the surface lies entirely on one side of the boundary plane, and what additional conclusions hold when C is convex?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2 (3*). Under what conditions on the boundary, a compact embedded cmc surface of R3 spanning a planar closed curve C is contained in one side of the boundary plane? and if C is convex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact embedded surface with non-empty boundary, having constant mean curvature $H \neq 0$ (a CMC surface), and assume that the boundary $\partial \Sigma = C$ is a closed Jordan curve lying in a plane $\Pi \subset \mathbb{R}^3$. The plane $\Pi$ divides $\mathbb{R}^3$ into two closed half-spaces $\Pi^+$ and $\Pi^-$. One says that $\Sigma$ lies on one side of $\Pi$ if $\Sigma \subset \Pi^+$ or $\Sigma \subset \Pi^-$.

(a) Determine geometric or topological hypotheses on the boundary curve $C$ (and possibly on $\Sigma$ near $C$, such as transversality conditions, contact-angle conditions with $\Pi$, or curvature/length conditions on $C$) that are sufficient to guarantee that every such compact embedded CMC surface $\Sigma$ spanning $C$ is contained entirely in one of the closed half-spaces determined by $\Pi$.

(b) Under the additional assumption that $C$ is a convex planar curve (i.e., $C$ bounds a convex region in $\Pi$), determine what further conclusions can be drawn about $\Sigma$: in particular, whether $\Sigma$ must be a topological disk, whether $\Sigma$ inherits the symmetries of $C$, and whether $\Sigma$ must be a graph over the planar domain bounded by $C$ or a spherical cap when $C$ is a circle.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of identifying sharp boundary hypotheses ensuring one-sidedness of compact embedded CMC surfaces with planar boundary remains an active research topic. Partial results exist: when the boundary is a circle and the surface lies on one side, it is a spherical cap (Brito-Earp-Meeks-Rosenberg and others); locally convex CMC hypersurfaces with strictly convex planar boundary lie in a half-space; recent work (e.g. 2024 paper on Special Weingarten surfaces with planar convex boundary) extends some conclusions, but a complete characterization of sufficient boundary conditions is not established.

status_evidence.title: Compact constant mean curvature surfaces in Euclidean three-space
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational results on compact embedded CMC surfaces with planar boundary, including conditions under which the surface lies on one side of the boundary plane.
status_evidence.claim: Classical partial results exist on one-sidedness for circular and convex planar boundaries.

status_evidence.title: Special Weingarten surfaces with planar convex boundary
status_evidence.snippet: A compact, connected, embedded Special Weingarten surface with planar convex boundary is a topological disk under suitable assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work continues to investigate one-sidedness and structural consequences for planar convex boundaries, indicating the problem is still being developed.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Locally convex embedded CMC hypersurfaces with strictly convex planar boundary lie in a half-space and inherit boundary symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: under local convexity and strict convexity of the boundary, one-sidedness holds.
